notes: Both of the refuter's readings are settled by the text. (1) OCCURS DEPENDING ON: a format 2 OCCURS 'does not imply that the length of the subject of the entry is variable, but that the number of occurrences is variable' (VI.5.8.4 GR2b), and a record is variable length only under a file or sort-merge description with RECORD VARYING (GR5). A CD record is neither, so its length is the fixed maximum, and a record whose maximum is 87 'describe[s] a record of exactly 87'. FUNCTION LENGTH's run-time answer of 3 is that function's own rule for a group with a variable occurrence item, not the record's length. The compiler accepts max 87 and refuses max 88 (cd1, cd2). (2) Condition-names: a condition-name entry is a data description entry, and the record description is 'the total set of data description entries associated with a particular record', so a later record whose 88 entry carries a VALUE clause contains a VALUE clause. 1985 states a condition-name exception where it intends one: REDEFINES SR9's 'must not contain any VALUE clauses, except in condition-name entries' shows that such an entry would otherwise count as containing one. SR5 has no such exception. The VALUE clause's own REDEFINES rule (VI.5.15.6 GR2) governs an entry that contains a REDEFINES clause, and that section is headed 'Data Description Entries Other Than Condition-Names'. The cross-reference '(See page VI-48, The VALUE Clause.)' points to the clause; it does not import an exception the CD rule leaves out. So COBOL6169 on an 88 in a later record is right, as kb/Work PB5290 (landed) decided. The 87-character count in standard data format characters is right on every probe.

next.reason: 1985: "Record description entries following an input CD entry implicitly redefine the record area established by the input CD entry"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the CD entry; the candidates cover only file, sort-merge, report and data description entries.". No 2023 clause holds the communication description entry, and no candidate covers record areas redefined by an input CD, so the 2023 standard lacks this feature.
